reference.stack: React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui + Rizum Glass

tokens.lightSurface: #FFFFFFF8; calibrated for GPUIX premultiplied Windows composition to visually match the web glass surface near #F8F8F7
tokens.systemControlOwnership: Windows platform adapter behind a React title-bar translation
tokens.nativeLegibilityCorrection: GPUIX body text and controls use an approximately 10% larger native metric than the browser reference after hands-on Windows review. Only the 14px contextual title is explicitly exempt; the surrounding title-bar geometry follows the product scale.
tokens.nativeLegibilityGeometry: Primary widths, control heights, icon hit targets, seek geometry, body insets, and content-sized window bounds move together. Typography receives an additional 0.5px optical correction where GPUIX rasterizes smaller. Radius, border, and shadow roles stay on the Rizum Glass rhythm instead of being mathematically scaled, so hierarchy does not inflate.
tokens.captionButtonGeometry: three 47px by 43px Windows slots; maximize disabled for the fixed-size utility
tokens.applicationIcon: The original mascot artwork remains unchanged. Its exterior tile follows the Windows 11 Fluent app-icon construction grid: a 2px exterior curve at the 48x48 reference size, equivalent to 52.25px on the 1254px source canvas. Every PNG-backed ICO layer is rasterized from the original artwork on its own target pixel grid, receives a supersampled target-size corner mask, and uses restrained small-layer sharpening below 64px; never create small layers by shrinking the already-masked master PNG. In addition to Windows' standard 16-256px targets, include 18px and 27px layers for the product's observed 112.5% custom scale. Bun's Windows executable resource path resamples custom ICO sizes, so the portable package preserves the generated ICO under assets and the Windows adapter loads exact taskbar and title-bar sizes from that sidecar through LoadImageW; PrivateExtractIconsW against the executable remains a graceful fallback. Assign ICON_SMALL and ICON_SMALL2 before ICON_BIG because the GPUIX window class otherwise lets the later small-icon assignment replace the taskbar slot.
tokens.windowOperations: The custom title band captures the pointer through Win32 and moves the window from global screen coordinates, including negative coordinates on monitors above or left of the primary display. Minimize and close remain native Win32 operations; Snap Layout is not claimed.
tokens.selectionOwnership: The application shell disables selection for static UI copy. Native input editors opt back into text selection explicitly; copy actions remain the primary affordance for generated playback URLs.
tokens.scrollOwnership: Fixed utility surfaces are not scroll containers when their complete task fits the content-sized window. Menus may scroll within their own bounded overlay; the settings and danmaku bodies do not react to the wheel.

states.name: empty-light
states.notes: The platform window is the only full-window glass surface. Its shared title-bar band carries the task title and Windows controls without a logo, ambient canvas, inner app card, or duplicate product identity.

states.name: ready-vod-light
states.notes: The default spike state exercises the densest main surface with one contextual task title and no duplicate product identity.

states.name: ready-vod-dark
states.notes: Dark appearance uses a solid neutral semantic remap.

components.primitive: GPUIX input + headless Select + interactive div controls

tokens.runtimeSeparator: The ready surface has three regions: source input, media routing with danmaku controls, and runtime output. Like the settings footer, the runtime row follows a quiet divider with 18px before and 14px after the line; no extra card or repeated section title is added. Its 32px minimum content box plus 2px vertical padding occupies 36px in GPUIX, and the content-sized window must preserve a separate 16px bottom safe area beneath that outer box.
tokens.runtimeTypography: Resolved playback URLs use Cascadia Mono 11.5px. Chinese preparation, routing, completion, stopped, and failure messages in the same stable row use Noto Sans SC 11.5px so missing CJK glyphs never fall through the Latin monospace face into an incidental system serif.
tokens.sectionMarkers: The ready surface follows one stable top-to-bottom marker sequence: source uses teal, media routing uses amber (#F59E0B in light appearance, #FBBF24 in dark appearance), danmaku uses violet, and runtime output uses rose. The Generate action icon matches the source marker. These colors identify content regions rather than transient health states; errors continue to be expressed by their local copy and action state.
tokens.playbackTransport: A compact 22px play/pause action shares the time row beneath the full-width 416px seek track. Newly generated relay-backed VOD starts prepared at 00:00: the stable publisher sends a still frame and silence while the user loads the address in VRChat, and the source clock begins only after Play. Pause uses the same hold path. Seek, part, and danmaku changes preserve that outer publisher, freeze the visible target position while preparing, and replace only the inner producer after its first output. At natural media completion the position remains at the end while the publisher sends the hold frame and silence for five minutes, so downstream playback buffers can drain before the address is released; direct URLs remain under VRChat player control.
tokens.partSelect: Render the full row only when the resolved video exposes at least two parts. A single-part video omits the label and selector, moves the seek control into the released space, and shortens the content-sized window. When shown, it uses the same 33px trigger, open-state border, chevron change, 220ms floating menu, row geometry, and selected check as the danmaku font selector. Trigger and menu labels own a bounded clipping region with ellipsis so long Bilibili titles cannot crowd the trailing chevron or panel edge.

states.name: ready-vod
states.notes: Includes part selection, seek adjustment, danmaku visibility, and copy output.

components.primitive: GPUIX input + motion segmented control + native file persistence

tokens.taskTitle: Noto Serif SC 14px semibold in the shared title-bar band
tokens.inputTypography: All settings values, including complete playback URLs, use Noto Sans SC 13px regular; monospace is reserved for comparable numeric playback data.
tokens.segmentedTypography: Noto Sans SC 12px regular with a fixed line box across every option; the 170px appearance control keeps the approved 64 / 42 / 42 proportions so the four-character system option retains relaxed side space after native legibility correction
tokens.buttonSurface: rgba(255,255,255,.84) in light appearance; native-composition calibration of the web control surface
tokens.sectionDividers: Horizontal section dividers use the surface-line color at 50% alpha; the two-column structural divider uses 55% alpha. Control outlines keep the solid surface-line token.
tokens.footerRhythm: The final settings action row uses 16px before its divider, 12px after the divider, a content-sized 33px action row, and a 16px bottom safe area measured from the control edge. The title entrance keeps its wider breathing room; the commit boundary closes more tightly without crowding the controls.
tokens.mediaRowSizing: Prototype rhythm: 18px section separation and 14px inset above the media status; 30px compact status row and 44px when download action, progress, or error detail is present
tokens.secretField: Masked by default with a compact trailing eye action; saved plaintext is requested from Rust only after explicit reveal
tokens.accountPopover: The QR login popover is bounded to the 188px account column: 170px content width, 10px inset, a 116px QR well, and compact status/footer copy. It must remain inside the product panel at every settings height.
tokens.connectionStatus: A compact worker-health status follows the playback address after the prototype's 10px field close plus 2px status offset, then retains 18px before the media section; it reports checking, available, or unavailable without duplicating local-persistence copy

states.name: settings-light
states.notes: The native 528px product window preserves the approved two-column proportions while applying the Windows hands-on legibility correction. Its height follows the visible media state: compact when FFmpeg is already available, expanded when download actions, progress, or error details are present.

states.name: settings-dark
states.notes: Dark appearance remaps the same neutral surfaces and keeps required captions at solid dark-caption contrast.

components.primitive: GPUIX motion segmented controls + headless Select + pointer slider + filter chips

tokens.previewSurface: A deterministic code-generated media field using Zen's layered-gradient construction and the user's Arc shell palette: coral #E39A9D with #EC6765 at the edge, warm neutral #CBC4B8, and teal #89E5DF with a stronger cyan-green edge. The faded browser-content whites are excluded; a separate fine-grain pass keeps the surface tactile.
tokens.previewClip: The outer media surface and backdrop share one 10px rounded path. The backdrop carries that radius directly because GPUIX 0.5.1 overflow clipping does not follow the parent's rounded path. The preview has no border; depth comes only from its quiet highlight and soft shadow.
tokens.previewMotion: The preview lines remain in the approved static positions. Continuous travel is deferred until GPUIX exposes reliable presentation-synchronized Windows motion.
tokens.rowGeometry: Within the 432px body width, every advanced row uses an 80px label column, a 12px gutter, and a 340px control column. Preview, controls, values, and hidden-type filters share the same right edge.
tokens.compactSelect: 33px trigger; 6px anchored offset; 4px menu inset; 31px option rows; 10px menu radius; floating glass uses the panel surface instead of the nested-region surface; selected-row tint is 4% semantic ink; open state changes the chevron direction and enters from -4px with the shared 220ms ease-out motion

states.name: danmaku-settings-light
states.notes: All advanced controls, including the hidden-type filters and bottom safe area, fit the native product window. The fixed utility body does not scroll; a future content expansion must establish a deliberate bounded body instead of leaking wheel movement into the whole surface.

states.name: danmaku-settings-dark
states.notes: The native preview stays a neutral near-black media surface in both appearances.

motion.reducedMotion: Render the final state immediately. GPUIX 0.5.1 uses opacity only because it does not expose a reliable transform motion primitive.
Same immediate semantic color and surface response. GPUIX motion cannot interpolate background color or transform in the pinned release.
Move the neutral capsule immediately while retaining selected-label contrast. Keyboard selection also resolves immediately.
Render immediately. The native fallback fades opacity without translating the surface or animating layout coordinates.

motion.from: previous copy, save, login, media, or relay state
motion.to: current state inside a stable shell
motion.reducedMotion: Replace content immediately while keeping the control or row geometry fixed. Continuously changing progress and seek values never crossfade.

materialFallbacks.webEffect: Application actions share an extended title-bar band beside platform controls.
materialFallbacks.gpuiStrategy: Use GPUIX transparent title-bar mode and a 42px React translation of the approved Single utility band. A Windows-only adapter forwards dragging, minimizing, and closing to Win32; the fixed-size utility keeps maximize disabled.
materialFallbacks.acceptedDifference: GPUIX 0.5.1 does not expose Windows caption geometry or native caption-button primitives, so this fixed-size utility reproduces their standard slots and native operations without Snap Layout.

materialFallbacks.webEffect: Per-panel backdrop-filter blur over an ambient radial presentation canvas
materialFallbacks.gpuiStrategy: Use GPUI window-level blur with a neutral translucent root surface, one quiet border, and a soft shadow.
materialFallbacks.acceptedDifference: GPUIX cannot reproduce CSS per-element refraction; the native surface is flatter and the browser canvas is intentionally omitted.

materialFallbacks.webEffect: CSS transforms for 1px hover lift and 0.97 press scale
materialFallbacks.gpuiStrategy: Use GPUIX native hover and active surface states without changing control geometry.
materialFallbacks.acceptedDifference: The first spike preserves semantic feedback but omits transform-based pointer motion.

materialFallbacks.webEffect: CSS text-shadow variants and transform-based continuous scrolling in the danmaku preview
materialFallbacks.gpuiStrategy: Use one foreground glyph run plus at most four bounded native offset copies for heavy/standard outline, or one offset copy for the 45-degree shadow, over a deterministic build asset composed from independent gradients and procedural grain. Keep both preview lines in fixed positions.
materialFallbacks.acceptedDifference: GPUIX 0.5.1 exposes neither gradient primitives, text-shadow, transform/repeat motion, nor a public presentation-synchronized frame callback. The build therefore rasterizes the backdrop algorithm once, keeps native font rasterization and a deliberately small outline layer count, and leaves the preview static until a reliable native motion path is available.
